v1_human_g2_ac.ac_1: Given available resources with fixed capacities then when requested amount is equal to its capacity function returns True
v1_human_g2_ac.ac_2: Given available resources with limited capacity when the total requested amount for any resource exceeds it's available capacity the function returns False
v1_human_g2_ac.ac_3: Given the inputs are provided when the format of inputs is not as expected the function returns a ValueError
v1_human_g2_ac.ac_4: Given a set of requests when function finds an invalid request it returns False
v1_human_g2_ac.ac_5: Given resources in decimals when total request amount does not exceed capacity then function returns True
v1_human_g2_ac.ac_6: Given resource & request values when values are valid and requested is less than max capacity then function returns True

v1_human_g2_constraints.c_2: The requests can be +ve or -ve number
v1_human_g2_constraints.c_3: The strings are only "cpu", "ram", "mem" for both request and resource
v1_human_g2_constraints.c_4: The formatting must be done as specified in comments (input parameter to function)
v1_human_g2_constraints.c_5: The s (resources & requests mapped is not returned only boolean
v1_human_g2_constraints.c_6: The resource, request values will never exceed max +ve int capacity

v1_human_g2_goal: The system is used to determine if a set of resource requests can be satisfied given limited capacity. Provided resources and requests, the objective is to map each request to a resource if and only if it is feasible
v1_human_g2_input:
request: List[Dict[str, Number]]: string like CPU, mem, ram mapped to the numbers
resource: Dict[str, Number]: same as above
v1_human_g2_output: The function returns True if all requests can be mapped to resources, no resource capacity exceeded, all capacities are valid, empty request list. False: Resource requested does not exist, total requested amount exceeds the capacity or requested amount. Value Error: only when the inputs are not in data structures as expected
